questions.prompt: A resource group must permit authorized configuration changes but reject accidental ARM deletion. Which lock fits?

options.explanation: It blocks deletion while permitting authorized updates.
It also blocks updates, contrary to the requirement.
A weaker role grant does not subtract existing delete permission.
A tag alone does not enforce deletion protection.

questions.prompt: A storage account has a CanNotDelete lock. A client has valid data-plane authorization to delete a blob. Does the account lock alone prevent that data operation?

options.text: No; management locks do not generally block data-plane blob deletion.
Yes; every byte under a locked account becomes immutable.
options.explanation: A management lock is not blob immutability.

options.text: Only blobs in Hot are protected by the lock.
options.explanation: Lock scope is not determined by access tier.

options.text: Only key2-authorized blob deletes are blocked.
options.explanation: The distinction is operation plane, not which account key is used.

questions.prompt: An Owner's ARM delete request fails because a resource has a Delete lock. What is the appropriate deliberate-deletion sequence?

options.text: Review and remove the lock with authorization, then delete the resource.
options.explanation: Owner does not silently bypass a still-effective lock.

options.text: Retry until Owner overrides the lock automatically.
options.explanation: Repeated identical requests do not remove the lock.
Reducing RBAC permission does not bypass the lock.

options.text: Change the resource group's metadata region.
options.explanation: That is not a lock-removal operation.
